---
name: feedback-never-kill-chrome-on-mac
description: Never pkill/restart Chrome on Nick's Mac — it's his live working browser; drive Interceptor against the running session only
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

While troubleshooting an Interceptor "no extensions connected" error (2026-07-15), I repeatedly `pkill -x "Google Chrome"` on the Mac and relaunched with different profiles. Nick was actively using Chrome and interrupted: "Your work is interrupting my chrome work instead of using the interceptor."

**Why:** The Mac's Chrome is Nick's live, logged-in working browser. Killing it destroys his open tabs/work mid-session. It is attributable, shared state — not my sandbox. (Same spirit as [[feedback-outbound-explicit-approval]]: everything in that browser is his.)

**How to apply:** Never `pkill`/restart Chrome or change its profiles on the Mac. If Interceptor can't see a window or extension: (1) try `interceptor tab new <url>` and re-check, (2) wait and retry — the extension reconnects lazily, (3) if still stuck, report the blocker to Nick and ask him to click/open something — he is often AT the machine. Work in one dedicated tab (`tab new`), keep focus-stealing minimal, close only that tab when done. The Interceptor extension lives in Chrome profile "Profile 3" (Outlook - Personal Work).

description: Nick does not want agents submitting third-party web forms even after approving the activity — collect information, draft, and stop before any submit
metadata:

Mid-way through an approved live-quote pull (2026-07-15, landlord insurance), Nick interrupted: "I don't want to submit forms, I want to collect information." This was AFTER he had said "yes get the live quotes" — his approval of an outcome did not extend to multi-step form submission as the method.

**Why:** Form funnels transmit his personal/property data step-by-step to third parties and are attributable to him. He wants information gathering (published rates, PDS facts, existing pages) separated from data-transmitting actions, which he does himself or approves per-step. Consistent with [[feedback-outbound-explicit-approval]] and the Interceptor PREFERENCES quick reference — treat multi-page quote/application funnels as a chain of outbound submits, not one approved action.

**How to apply:** When a task seems to need a web form (quotes, signups, applications), default to: collect what is publicly readable, prefill/draft at most, and surface the form to Nick to submit. If a funnel's early steps were already progressed, stop where you are, submit nothing further, and report what was entered. Ask before starting any funnel by naming the data it will transmit.
